name: 4-Aryl-oxazolidin-2-one, sulfone-capped diaryl ether
head: oxazolidin-2-one
ec50_basis: the only neutral head that reproduces the measured 2.22 A geminal pair; carbonyl distal acceptor at pK_BHX 2.3-2.6 against the carboxylate's 4.3-4.8, i.e. a 2-3 kcal/mol deficit spread over two contacts, anchored on OEA's measured 120 nM-3 uM
selectivity_strategy: geometric: hold the acceptor span at 2.2-2.3 A. Measured here, PPARgamma's engaged acceptors span 4.46 A, so a tight geminal pair is intrinsically alpha-shaped. Against delta, which also takes a tight pair (3TKM, 2.10 A), geometry gives nothing - delta must be bought on arm II sterics and counter-screened
breaks_first: PPARdelta selectivity. Delta's cage accepts the same tight geminal pair this head is built around, delta is the most abundant retinal PPAR, and it is pro-angiogenic
rationale: the lead. Best measured geometric match of any neutral head (2.29 A against a required 2.22 +/- 0.06), permanently neutral, and the methylsulfonyl sits on the distal vector where polarity lowers logD without touching arm I

name: alpha,alpha-Dimethyl sulfonylmethyl aryl ether
head: methyl sulfone
ec50_basis: geminal S-O pair at 2.52 A is inside the measured window, but sulfonyl oxygens are weak acceptors (pK_BHX 1.3-1.6), the largest basicity deficit of any competent head. Potency is projected low and the range is wide
selectivity_strategy: none from the head - a weak symmetric acceptor pair discriminates nothing. Selectivity must come entirely from arm II/III sterics, which is the weakest selectivity position of the five
breaks_first: potency. A 3 kcal/mol acceptor deficit against a receptor whose incumbent ligands are already only 1-30 nM is unlikely to be recovered from the arms alone
rationale: the cheapest test of the geometric hypothesis. Permanently neutral, smallest competent neutral head at 1.46x the carboxylate, trivially synthesised from the fibrate body. Its value is as an experiment, not as a candidate

name: Methyl phosphonamidate, biaryl ether body
head: phosphonamidate
ec50_basis: P=O is the strongest neutral acceptor available (pK_BHX 3.0-3.5), a deficit of only ~1.3 units against the carboxylate. Offsetting that, the computed geminal span is 2.58 A - outside the measured window, so some of the advantage is spent on strain
selectivity_strategy: the P centre is stereogenic, so the two P-substituents can be used to probe arm I asymmetry directly - a selectivity handle none of the carbon heads has
breaks_first: the span. 2.58 A is 0.36 A wide of the measured requirement and a tetrahedral P cannot be compressed the way an sp2 carbon can. After that, metabolic and hydrolytic stability of the P-N bond
rationale: the highest-information scaffold in the set and the one nobody has tried at any PPAR. Strongest neutral acceptors, lowest protein binding of the five, not an OATP1B recognition element

name: Fibrate acid retained, lipophilicity stripped
head: carboxylate (control arm)
ec50_basis: the head is the validated one, so potency is set by the body. Stripping the lipophilic arm costs affinity against pemafibrate but the chemotype's SAR transfers directly
selectivity_strategy: the carboxylate is itself part of alpha selectivity, which is the strongest starting position of the five
breaks_first: nothing in the chemistry - the exposure. It is still an anion, so OATP1B hepatic uptake and MRP/BCRP efflux at the barrier both persist. This arm exists to show what the acid can and cannot do once lipophilicity is removed as a confound
rationale: the control. If this closes the exposure gap, no neutral head is needed and the programme is a medicinal-chemistry tidy-up rather than a new chemotype. It is included to be falsified

name: Fibrate hydroxamic acid, benzophenone removed
head: hydroxamic acid
ec50_basis: chelating O,O pair, smallest competent head at 1.27x the carboxylate, but the computed span is 2.64 A - outside the measured window - so the H12 contact is modelled as lost
selectivity_strategy: footprint. At 1.27x it is the only neutral head small enough to exploit alpha's arm I being tighter than gamma's
breaks_first: off-target metal chelation. A hydroxamate is a zinc binder: HDAC, the matrix metalloproteinases and carbonic anhydrase are all in range, and MMP inhibition in retina is not a neutral liability. Hydroxamate mutagenicity via Lossen rearrangement is the second
rationale: included because it is the smallest neutral competent head and the footprint argument is the one the source analysis leaned on. Carried with its liabilities stated rather than quietly dropped
